hooks.text: Astronomers once believed our single galaxy was the entire universe.
Every distant galaxy is moving away from Earth right now.
Trillions of galaxies were once thought to be zero.

title: How One Astronomer Proved the UNIVERSE Is Expanding
description: Before Edwin Hubble's observations, astronomers believed the Milky Way was the entire cosmos. His work proved distant galaxies are moving away in an expanding universe.

beats.text: Astronomers once believed our single galaxy was the entire universe.
beats.visual: Illustration of the Milky Way galaxy in dark space

beats.text: Faint misty patches in space seemed to be simple gas clouds.
beats.visual: Early astronomical photographic plate of faint spiral nebulae

beats.text: Former high school Spanish teacher Edwin Hubble decided to inspect them.
beats.visual: Photograph of Edwin Hubble at Carnegie Mount Wilson Observatory

beats.text: Using California's 100-inch Hooker Telescope, he measured distant pulsing stars.
beats.visual: The 100-inch Hooker Telescope at Mount Wilson Observatory

beats.text: Hubble proved Andromeda was a separate galaxy far outside our own.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Andromeda Galaxy M31 core

beats.text: He then tracked light from far galaxies shifting toward red wavelengths.
beats.visual: Diagram of galaxy redshift optical light spectrum

beats.text: Farther galaxies receded faster, proving the universe is actively expanding.
beats.visual: Diagram of the expanding universe and receding galaxies

beats.text: Albert Einstein visited Mount Wilson and called static space his biggest blunder.
beats.visual: Photograph of Albert Einstein and Edwin Hubble at Mount Wilson, 1931
queries: Albert Einstein Edwin Hubble Mount Wilson

beats.text: Until then, no one knew other galaxies even existed.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope view of deep field galaxies
